newsitem.title: CHINA: China anti-Japan activist sent out of Beijing.
newsitem.headline: China anti-Japan activist sent out of Beijing.

text.p: Chinese officials told a leading anti-Japanese activist to leave Beijing on Sunday after he tried to organise a protest against Tokyo's control over a group of disputed islands in the East China Sea, friends said.
Activist Tong Zeng left Beijing accompanied by a colleague at around midday on Sunday, said a friend and fellow campaigner who declined to be identified.
He appeared to have been sent to Qinghai region in China's remote northwest, a friend said. It was not clear how long he would have to spend away from the capital.
Tong had earlier said he was determined to stay in Beijing despite pressure from officials. "He definitely wasn't willing to go...he had no choice," said another friend.
Tong was warned by officials last week to halt a campaign for military action against Tokyo's presence in the Diaoyu islands, known as the Senkakus in Japanese.

On Friday he shelved plans for a demonstration outside the Japanese embassy on September 18, the anniversary of the 1931 start of the Sino-Japanese war, after failing to give police the required five day's notice.
The Diaoyu dispute flared after a group of rightwing Japanese built a lighthouse in July on one of the uninhabited but potentially resource-rich islands.

Outrage over Japan's refusal to tear down the Diaoyu lighthouse has united nationalist sentiment in Beijing as well as in its arch-rival Taiwan. Even democratic activists in Hong Kong have joined calls for tough action from China.
Beijing's Communist Party-controlled media quickly condemns any perceived signs of resurgent Japanese militarism, but China has in the past suppressed unofficial protests against Tokyo.

Tong's high-profile anti-Japanese campaigns led authorities to confiscate his passport and exile him temporarily from Beijing during the U.N.-sponsored World Conference on Women in September last year.
